evidence: Across 68 held-out weekly releases at 5 review slots, 83.2% of first-release alerts and 89.7% of revision-adjusted alerts appeared in the next release's residence-based list.
next_decision: Keep first-publication alerts provisional. Actual review budgets and the observed cost of a one-release delay determine whether an adjusted list is useful.
boundary: The advance column is reported by liable state and includes a workshare proxy. The next release uses state of residence. The ranked target is a later published measure, not a directly observed employment shock.
